title: Fixed
caption: Fixed 🙂 An animated story about a town where sadness is against the law. Would you be able to fake it? #animatedstory #storytime #blockmated

shots.text: In our town, sadness is against the law.
The streetlights have little cameras in them.
They watch your face.
Frown three times in one week, and a white van comes for you at night.
You come back fixed.
Fixed people are lovely.
They're polite. They hold doors. They never complain.
Mr. Daly next door got fixed in 2017.
He waves at mailboxes.
He waves at the rain.
Mom got fixed when I was five.
She's been lovely ever since.
There are two ways to spot a fixed person.
They blink exactly once every ten seconds.
And they say thank you to everything. Even walls.
On Monday, my best friend Teo moved away.
His desk was empty by lunch.
I frowned twice before the bell rang.
I practised smiling in the bathroom mirror until my cheeks shook.
On Wednesday, I found his name carved under his desk.
Strike three.
That night, the white van parked outside our house.
Mom opened the door before they knocked.
The Clinic was the whitest room I've ever seen.
Everyone in it was smiling.
A nurse handed me a little cup of something pink.
Drink up, she said.
Then she said thank you to the cup.
I pretended to swallow.
When she blinked, I spat it into a plant.
In the morning, I did what I'd seen.
Smile.
Blink every ten seconds.
Thank the walls.
They sent me home fixed.
For a whole year, I pretended.
Nobody noticed. Not my teacher.
Not the cameras.
Not Mom.
Then one night, I came downstairs for water.
Mom was alone in the kitchen, crying into a dish towel.
Without a sound.
And blinking, exactly once every ten seconds.
She'd been pretending so long, she did it even when nobody was watching.
She wiped her face, smiled at the fridge, and whispered: thank you.
The pink stuff doesn't work.
It never did.
Nobody in our town is fixed.
We're all just very good at smiling.
I'm smiling right now.
So is everyone in our town.
